title: [KBM] Improve labeling for NumPad non 0-9 keys (#21375)

review.body_prefix:
### Qualified current-revision assessment

The changed layout map gives the non-digit numpad keys distinct display labels, keeps the layout-derived decimal character when available, and removes the duplicate bare Divide entry while retaining its numpad-origin identity. Stored key codes are not replaced by the new display text.

The exact affected native test project builds with analyzers enabled, and both added label/list regression tests pass. The map update immediately assigns the final decimal label; no intervening presence-sensitive consumer is established. The complete list-generation path and passing regression contradict a current disappearance of Divide. Sharing the test constant is optional refactoring, not a demonstrated key-identity mismatch.

No additional required correction is established in that inspected scope. This is a qualified assessment, not fresh zero-finding approval or complete keyboard-remapping, alternate-layout, shortcut, or application UI signoff.

The current source trace confirms the full virtual-key population loop precedes the decimal read, and the tagged divide map entry is added by the numpad enumeration. The test bit is the DWORD-representable constant0x80000000; the retained exact affected build and both new tests pass. Optional map-access/constant-style changes are not required corrections.
